context: Stochastic effects limit for radiation workers; effective dose averaged over 5 years; single year max 50 mSv; below limit causing deterministic effects (>100 mGy threshold)
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl liquidators: many received this in a few hours to days in 1986; 530000 workers total avg 117 mSv (6x annual limit); some received 1000+ mGy in one shift (>50x annual limit)

timeframe: annual; revised downward from 150 mSv in ICRP 118 2012
context: Revised down from 150 mSv/yr after epidemiological evidence of cataract at lower doses; relevant for Chernobyl liquidators (many developed radiation cataracts)
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl liquidators: cataracts documented at doses >0.5-1 Gy; UNSCEAR 2008 notes many liquidators received equivalent doses >20x new annual limit

context: Deterministic threshold for skin is ~2000 mGy; 500 mSv limit ensures low probability of deterministic effects; shallow personal dose equivalent Hp(0.07)
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl ARS patients: skin doses 400-500 Gy on some patients (1000x annual limit in hours); skin burns were major cause of at least 19 of 28 ARS deaths

context: Public dose limit for planned exposure situations; excludes background and medical; principle: ALARA (as low as reasonably achievable) means doses should be below this in practice
chernobyl_comparison: Prypiat current: 4.932 µSv/h = ~43 mSv/yr = 43x public limit → uninhabitable; Chornobyl city: 0.209 µSv/h = ~1.8 mSv/yr; approaching limit for habitation

context: Lower emergency reference level (ERL); below this: no protective action recommended based on dose alone; interventions at higher doses become justified
chernobyl_comparison: Soviet evacuation of Pripyat 36 hours after accident likely resulted in doses >20 mSv for many residents in first 36 hours from external and internal I-131

context: Upper ERL; above this: protective actions (evacuation KI shelter) always justified; below 20 mSv: not generally justified from radiation standpoint; 20-100 mSv: judgment required
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl: Soviet 30-km evacuation decision based on arbitrary zone not individual dose assessment; many outside 30 km received more than those inside; KI was protective action that could have helped

context: EU limit for Cs-137 in most foods (meat fish dairy vegetables) for non-infant non-baby-food consumption; in effect since 1987 (initially at 370 Bq/kg); relaxed post-emergency
chernobyl_comparison: Wild boar mean 46000 Bq/kg = 37x EU limit; max 660000 = 528x; catfish 50000 = 40x; food restrictions on some European mushrooms/wild game still active 2024

context: Lower limit for infant food dairy products baby food; reflects higher dose coefficient for infants (4.4E-08 Sv/Bq vs adult 1.3E-08)
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl 1986: Soviet milk ban delayed 2-3 weeks; Poland immediately restricted infant milk when Cs-137 exceeded 370 Bq/L

context: I-131 in milk and dairy; limit relevant during first weeks of accident; thyroid dose driver
chernobyl_comparison: USSR delay in implementing milk ban in 1986 was primary prevention failure for thyroid cancer; Poland implemented ban at 370 Bq/L I-131 within days

context: Sr-90 limit much lower than Cs-137 per Bq because Sr-90 is a bone-seeker with higher dose coefficient; 125 Bq/kg in food; 125 Bq/L in beverages
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl: Sr-90 in Pripyat River exceeded this immediately post-accident; Sr-90 in some CEZ groundwater wells still exceeds by >100x in 2024

context: Much lower than EU limit; Japan lowered from 500 to 100 Bq/kg after Fukushima; reflects precautionary approach; harmonized with EU for fish to 1250 Bq/kg
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl wild boar 46000 Bq/kg vs Japanese limit 100 = 460x; European wild game restrictions show EU 1250 limit still often exceeded decades later

context: Approximate threshold for clinical ARS (Grade I) signs; bone marrow depression; nausea vomiting in majority of people exposed; below this: no clinical ARS; above this: treatment required

context: LD50/30 = dose causing 50% mortality within 30 days without treatment; with full BMT and supportive care can extend to ~6-8 Gy
chernobyl_comparison: Chernobyl Grade IV ARS (6-16 Gy): 21 patients 20 deaths even with BMT; LD100 essentially reached at ~10-12 Gy based on Chernobyl experience

context: Natural background from cosmic rays + terrestrial gamma + Rn-222 + internal (K-40 C-14); range 1-10 mSv/yr globally; Ramsar Iran ~100 mSv/yr from high-Ra groundwater

context: Rn-222 (and daughters) = largest single natural radiation source to human population; accounts for ~53% of natural background; lung cancer risk; Rn in homes varies 10-10000 Bq/m3

regulatory_body: ICRP 103 2007 recommended for radiation protection purposes
context: LNT: any dose however small has proportional risk of cancer; used as conservative tool for radiation protection; does NOT mean all doses are dangerous; basis for ICRP 100 mSv/yr occupational limit
